title: Role Handoff Lighthouse & Probe Lab (14d)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, pragmatic working doc for candidate-to-contributor transitions where we need to: (1) accelerate ramp in the first 14 days, (2) collect consistent interview evidence for final hiring decisions, and (3) provide a low-friction mentor pairing + handoff routine for small teams (1–3 engineers). Use for contract-to-perm trials, part-time hires, and high-velocity IC hiring lanes.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- 14-day micro-sprint called the Lighthouse + Probe Lab.
- Focus: 3 core outcomes: onboarding safety (access + baseline runbook), technical competency signal (pairing + probe), and cultural/communication baseline (async updates + debrief).
- Light-weight rubric used by interviewers + mentor to score readiness at day 7 and day 14.

Why this exists (notes to self):
- Many current playbooks assume long ramp/higher headcount support. Small pods need a repeatable, minimal overhead flow.
- We want to avoid long open loops for contract trials — faster evidence collection, clearer decision triggers.

Hiring plan (for a single contributor pod):
- Role: Senior Platform Engineer (example).
- Hiring runway: 3 interview stages (screen, technical pairing, manager + culture) + Lighthouse trial offer (2 week paid trial).
- Offer framework: trial compensation = prorated weekly pay; conversion bonus on full hire (optional).
- Ramp expectation: by day 14 candidate should complete 2 scoped tickets, demonstrate repo familiarity, and show one small infra improvement suggestion.

Interview rubric (single-page, shorthand):
- Domains: Problem decomposition (PD), Code fluency (CF), System design at pod scale (SD), Communication & async habits (CA), Security/ops awareness (SO).
- Scoring: 1–5 (1 = no signal / fail, 3 = meets baseline, 5 = exceptional).
- Minimum passing cut: PD >=3, CF >=3, at least one of SD or SO >=3, CA >=3.
- Evidence anchors (what to write in notes):
  - PD: example where candidate split a vague ticket into 3 focused tasks; asked clarifying questions; sketched acceptance criteria.
  - CF: made small edits, ran tests, explained tradeoffs, code clarity.
  - SD: understood operational constraints (batching, cache, KV spill), articulated rollout/fallback plan.
  - CA: uses clear headings, links PRs/Jira, flags risk early.
  - SO: mentions threat model, minimal secrets handling, and CI checks.

Pairing & probe session (technical stage -> used in trial):
- 90m pairing exercise (remote or in-person): 15m context + 60m coding/infra pairing + 15m debrief.
- Script:
  1) Quick context (owner/stack/constraints).
  2) Candidate writes one small end-to-end change (example: add a health-check + metric to service X).
  3) Encourage candidate to run locally / add unit test / open a draft PR template.
  4) Mentor observes prompts, blockers, and how candidate asks for clarifications.
- Probe lab ticket examples (deliverable in trial):
  - Fix flaky CI step that blocks deploys (small, obvious fix).
  - Implement a lightweight metrics dashboard for a single endpoint.
  - Migrate a job from cron to scheduled task runner (scope 2–4 hours).

Preboarding checklist (to be completed before day 0 / day 1 start):
- Accounts: SSO invite, GitHub org access, Jira access, Okta groups, Google drive folders.
- Access: dev cluster read-only, staging write, prod read (escalate only as needed).
- Hardware: allocate loaner laptop if remote; VPN client + instructions.
- Security: NDA signed, basic security training link, KMS guidance TBD.
- Meet & greet: calendar block for intro standup, mentor + manager 30m, buddy lunch (optional).
- Communication expectations doc link: add to candidate + mentor calendar.

Day-by-day (high level):
- Day 0: Finalize access, run local dev bootstrap, intro channel join.
- Day 1–3: Small onboarding tasks (dev env, run tests, first repo PR - trivial).
- Day 4–7: First probe ticket in pairing mode; mid-point check-in (manager + mentor).
- Day 8–10: Independent work on second ticket, weekly demo prep.
- Day 11–13: Polish docs, run retro with mentor, prepare day-14 demo.
- Day 14: Demo to pod + hiring committee signal. Decision window opens same day.

Mentor shadow schedule (typical week):
- 1.5 hours/day pairing early days (D1–D7), then drop to 45m/day (D8–D14).
- Daily async: candidate posts 3 bullet update in channel (what I did, blockers, plan).
- Mentor note: annotate PRs with clear, time-bound feedback.

Success metrics (what we measure to convert):
- Behavioral: consistent async updates, minimal blocker escalation, starts and finishes scoped tickets.
- Technical: PRs have CI green, tests added or preserved, no major security misses.
- Team fit: attends ceremonies, communicates effectively, reasonable ramp velocity compared to peers.
- Risk tolerance: if candidate requires >2 critical unblockings per week, pause conversion.

Decision triggers and risk signals (escalation):
- Immediate fail: major security blind spot (exposing secrets), or destructive infra change without review.
- Pause + remediation: repeated missing of basic access tasks (not bootstrapped by D2), repeated no-shows.
- Convert: meets all success metrics and mentor recommends.

Sample evaluation snapshot (what to paste into final notes):
- PD: 4 — broke problem into tidy steps, asked clarifying Qs.
- CF: 3 — minor formatting + test gaps, but runnable change.
- SD: 3 — pragmatic, noted rollback plan.
- CA: 4 — clear updates + links.
- SO: 3 — basic threats covered.
- Summary: Strong fit for small pod, recommend conversion with standard ramp plan.

Admin / logistics (short):
- Trial pay approval: People Ops needs to approve per-case (link HR-482).
- Equipment ordering: tag purchase request with "lighthouse-equipment".
- Legal: attach trial agreement to candidate offer doc.

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Should trials always be paid? (currently yes; reduce bias + faster onboarding).
- Standard conversion bonus — figure out threshold (TBD with finance).
- Can we formalize a 1-pager that sits in offer emails? (create template).
- Investigate automating preboarding invites (Okta + GitHub flow).

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally concise; operationalize the rubric into a single Google form (one-click scoring) — tracked to HR-482.
- Keep probe tickets intentionally small (<=4h) so we surface blockers quickly.
- Use Slack thread naming convention: "#lighthouse-<candidate-last>-<role>" for transparency.

References / quick links:
- Confluence: /team-ops/lighthouse-onboard (draft)
- Jira: HR-482 (trial offer flow)
- Example probe ticket: github.com/redwood-inference/internal/issues/657

Revision history:
- 2025-11-05 initial draft (Ava)
- 2025-11-09 updated rubric anchors + pairing script (Diego)
- 2025-11-12 added decision triggers and open question list (Sofia)

---
Notes to self: keep this doc short, pragmatic, and keep iterating after 5 hires.
